subject: chemistry
title: Measurement & Data Processing Adventure 3: SI units, sig figs and graphical analysis
welcome_lead: Today you'll standardise units, count significant figures, and read straight-line graphs.
meta_desc: IBDP Chemistry — SI units, prefixes, significant figures, graphs, R², slope and intercept.
final_note: You learned 7 SI base units underpin chemistry, prefixes scale them, sig figs reflect measurement precision, and y = mx + c reveals slope and intercept.

concepts.def: m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd

walkthroughs.body_html:
7 base units: m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd.

Derived: N (kg m/s²), J (N m), Pa (N/m²), V (J/C), Ω (V/A).

Prefixes: pico (10⁻¹²), nano (10⁻⁹), micro (10⁻⁶), milli (10⁻³), kilo (10³), mega (10⁶), giga (10⁹).

1 mol/dm³ = 1000 mol/m³ — careful with volumes!

Rules: all non-zero digits significant; zeros between or trailing after decimal significant.

- 0.00540 — 3 sf.
- 540 — 2 or 3 sf (ambiguous; 5.40×10² unambiguous).
- 540.0 — 4 sf.

When multiplying/dividing: result has sig figs of least precise.
When adding/subtracting: result has decimal places of least precise.

Linearise to y = mx + c when possible.

Arrhenius: ln k = -Ea/R · (1/T) + ln A.

Beer-Lambert: A = εcl → slope vs c gives ε for known l.

R² close to 1 → good linear fit. Use best-fit, NOT joining the dots. Indicate uncertainties with error bars; min/max gradient gives slope uncertainty.
